program:
mnist: a network of 784 pixels, 32 tanh units and 10 digits learning handwritten digits, by Adam or by damped Newton steps, then tested.
Data: the MNIST database of handwritten digits (Yann LeCun, Corinna Cortes and Christopher J. C. Burges), Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 3.0; not kept with the program, read from the four files where you put them.
Prior art: backpropagation (Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams, 1986; reverse-mode differentiation, Linnainmaa, 1970); Adam (Diederik Kingma and Jimmy Ba, "Adam: a method for stochastic optimization", ICLR 2015); Hessian-free optimization (James Martens, ICML 2010) with conjugate gradients stopped at negative curvature (Trond Steihaug, 1983) and Levenberg-Marquardt damping (Levenberg, 1944; Marquardt, 1963); exact Hessian-vector products (Barak Pearlmutter, "Fast exact multiplication by the Hessian", 1994), here forward over backward with dual numbers, as JAX's hvp does.
Adapted: the minimal standard generator (Stephen K. Park and Keith W. Miller, CACM 31(10), 1988) for the starting weights, scaled by the square root of each unit's inputs (LeCun, Bottou, Orr and Müller, "Efficient BackProp", 1998).
